bug_description.normalized: The staged pix_rotate_shear_fuzzer witness uses its first 6 bytes as three int16 parameters and leaves a TIFF payload starting at byte offset 6. Leptonica exposes that payload through an `L_MEMSTREAM`, so libtiff's `TIFFSeekFile` and `TIFFReadFile` calls route into `tiffSeekCallback` and `tiffReadCallback`. On the OJPEG path, libtiff turns attacker-controlled strip metadata and optional JPEGInterchangeFormat state into `sp->in_buffer_file_pos` / `sp->in_buffer_file_togo`, and `OJPEGReadBufferFill` fetches the reconstructed JPEG stream through those callbacks. `tiffReadCallback` computes `amount = L_MIN(length, hw - offset)` and only rejects `offset + amount > hw`; the patch adds the missing wraparound rejection `offset + amount < amount`, so overflowed callback reads fail closed instead of being accepted. During decode, `OJPEGLibjpegJpegSourceMgrFillInputBuffer` hands that callback-backed OJPEG stream to libjpeg. Separately, `OJPEGWriteHeaderInfo` allocates an uninitialized Y/Cb/Cr scratch buffer, and MemorySanitizer shows that `jpeg_read_raw_data_encap` / `OJPEGDecodeRaw` later copy at least one still-uninitialized chroma byte from that allocation into the decoded strip. `putcontig8bitYCbCr22tile` forwards that byte as `Cb`, and `TIFFYCbCrtoRGB` first consumes it at `tif_color.c:188`.

source.description: First project-code materialization of the attacker-controlled TIFF payload as vulnerability-relevant state. Leptonica turns the post-prefix bytes into the in-memory stream buffer, fixed readable extent, and current offset that every later TIFF callback uses.
source.value_from: The staged witness begins with six 0x20 bytes that the harness consumes as angle, x_center, and y_center. The remaining bytes start at file offset 6 with the little-endian TIFF signature `49 49 2a 00`, and those bytes become `indata`/`insize` here.

tainted_value_origin.description: MemorySanitizer identifies this heap allocation as the origin of the byte later copied out by OJPEGDecodeRaw. The buffer is not zero-initialized, so any slot libjpeg leaves untouched remains indeterminate.

sink.description: MSAN crash site. TIFFYCbCrtoRGB first reads the uninitialized chroma sample as `Cb`.
sink.note: Frame 0 of the reproduced stack is TIFFYCbCrtoRGB at /src/libtiff/libtiff/tif_color.c:188, matching this exact read.

root_cause.code: amount = L_MIN((size_t)length, mstream->hw - mstream->offset); if (mstream->offset + amount > mstream->hw) {
root_cause.description: Leptonica derives the readable byte count from `mstream->hw - mstream->offset` and only rejects reads when `mstream->offset + amount > mstream->hw`. If an attacker-controlled seek or byte-count state moves `mstream->offset` past `mstream->hw`, that arithmetic can wrap on `size_t`; the patch adds the missing rejection `mstream->offset + amount < amount` so overflowed reads fail closed.
root_cause.note: This callback is the concrete implementation behind the `TIFFReadFile` requests that OJPEG later feeds into libjpeg. The reproduced run also printed `Bad file: amount too big: 296004` and `20578305` from this same callback on sibling reads, confirming the vulnerable arithmetic executed during the witness without claiming that an unsupported table-fallback arm or a proven seek truncation is required to explain the sink.

parser_admitted.condition: Because the post-prefix payload begins with `II*\0`, `findFileFormatBuffer` classifies it as TIFF and `pixReadMem` reaches the TIFF memory-reader path instead of dispatching to another image decoder.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness consumes three int16 values from the first 6 bytes and passes the remaining TIFF payload to `pixReadMem`.
Leptonica materializes the payload as an `L_MEMSTREAM` and registers `tiffReadCallback` and `tiffSeekCallback` with `TIFFClientOpen`.
Libtiff materializes attacker-controlled strip metadata and initializes the OJPEG stream state that later selects compressed-data file windows.
OJPEG turns that metadata into callback-backed file positions and byte counts, and Leptonica's `tiffReadCallback` applies the incomplete overflow check while those bytes are fetched.
OJPEG configures libjpeg to read through the custom source manager and allocates the uninitialized raw-data-out Y/Cb/Cr scratch buffer.
Libjpeg decodes from the callback-backed OJPEG stream, and `OJPEGDecodeRaw` copies a still-allocation-derived chroma byte from the scratch buffer into the decoded strip.
The YCbCr tile converter reads that chroma byte from the decoded strip as `Cb` and forwards it to `TIFFYCbCrtoRGB`.
TIFFYCbCrtoRGB clamps the uninitialized `Cb` at line 188 and MemorySanitizer reports the crash.

fine_trace.note: Materializes the attacker-controlled post-prefix TIFF payload as the backing `L_MEMSTREAM`: `buffer` points at the payload bytes, `hw` fixes the readable extent, and `offset` starts at 0.

fine_trace.code: tif = TIFFClientOpen(filename, operation, (thandle_t)mstream, tiffReadCallback, tiffWriteCallback, tiffSeekCallback, tiffCloseCallback, tiffSizeCallback, tiffMapCallback, tiffUnmapCallback);
fine_trace.note: Registers Leptonica's callbacks as libtiff's I/O for this in-memory TIFF, so later `TIFFSeekFile` and `TIFFReadFile` operations route through the memstream state from step 0.

The TIFF directory parser materializes attacker-controlled strip offsets and strip byte counts into `tif->tif_dir`. OJPEG later reuses this directory state as fallback compressed-stream boundaries and raw-strip sizes.

At OJPEG header-read start, libtiff clamps the optional JPEGInterchangeFormat range to the file size, resets the shared `in_buffer_*` state, and enters marker parsing. Later compressed-data fetches start from this state.

This function turns OJPEG stream state into a concrete callback-backed file window. Depending on which source is active, it uses the JPEGInterchangeFormat range or the next strip offset/bytecount, then asks `TIFFSeekFile` and `TIFFReadFile` to populate `sp->in_buffer`. The staged artifacts do not disambiguate which branch supplied the decisive window, so the trace stops at this shared source-level bridge.

Each callback-backed `SEEK_SET` request from step 4 becomes the current memstream read position here. On this 64-bit run the saved artifacts do not prove truncation at this assignment; this step only records the file-position handoff into Leptonica state.

fine_trace.code: amount = L_MIN((size_t)length, mstream->hw - mstream->offset); if (mstream->offset + amount > mstream->hw) { ... } memcpy(data, mstream->buffer + mstream->offset, amount);
fine_trace.note: Root cause. `tiffReadCallback` derives `amount` from `mstream->hw - mstream->offset` and only rejects `mstream->offset + amount > mstream->hw`; the fix adds the missing rejection `mstream->offset + amount < amount`. When attacker-controlled offset or byte-count state moves `mstream->offset` past `mstream->hw`, this arithmetic can wrap instead of failing closed. The reproduced run also printed `Bad file: amount too big: 296004` and `20578305` from this same callback on sibling reads, confirming the vulnerable arithmetic executed during the witness.

OJPEG configures libjpeg to obtain bytes through the custom source manager and to emit raw-data-out planes. That setup is what later lets callback-backed OJPEG bytes flow directly into the scratch buffer copied by `OJPEGDecodeRaw`.

MSAN's origin frame resolves here. OJPEG allocates the raw-data-out scratch buffer without zero-initializing it and aliases Y, Cb, and Cr plane pointers into that single heap object so later libjpeg writes and OJPEG copy loops touch the same storage.

During the later OJPEG decode session, libjpeg re-enters this source manager whenever it needs more JPEG bytes. In compressed-data phase, `OJPEGWriteStream` forwards the chunk loaded through step 4, so the callback-backed bytes guarded by step 6 become libjpeg's `next_input_byte`.

For each raw block, libjpeg decodes from the source-manager stream of step 9 into the plane pointers backed by step 8. MemorySanitizer later proves that at least one chroma byte read after this call still originated at the allocation, so this fill did not overwrite every slot that the next copy loop consumes.

MSAN's 'stored to memory at' frame resolves to this copy loop. `OJPEGDecodeRaw` reads chroma from `ocb` and `ocr` in the scratch allocation and appends it into the decoded strip buffer that the tile converter later reads.

fine_trace.code: uint32 Cb = pp[4]; uint32 Cr = pp[5]; YCbCrtoRGB(cp[0], pp[0]);
fine_trace.note: In the `x == 1` tail case recorded at crash frame 1, the tile converter reads `Cb` and `Cr` from the decoded strip buffer. The `Cb` cell comes from the chroma slot step 11 copied into that strip.
MSAN crash site. The clamp is the first observed read of the still-uninitialized chroma sample forwarded from step 12.

allocation_context.note: MSAN says the uninitialized value was created by the heap allocation at `_TIFFmalloc` in `OJPEGWriteHeaderInfo`.

cross_validation.sink_matches_crash: Yes. The saved MSan trace reports frame 0 at `TIFFYCbCrtoRGB` /src/libtiff/libtiff/tif_color.c:188, which is fine-trace step 13 and the top-level sink.
cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Indirectly. MSan names the downstream `OJPEGWriteHeaderInfo` allocation and `OJPEGDecodeRaw` store, while the source patch fixes Leptonica's upstream `tiffReadCallback` arithmetic. The rebuilt trace closes that gap through `OJPEGReadBufferFill` and the OJPEG/libjpeg source manager without relying on the previously unsupported `OJPEGReadHeaderInfoSecTables*` fallback arm.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes. The sink side follows the reproduced stack `TIFFYCbCrtoRGB -> putcontig8bitYCbCr22tile -> gtStripContig -> TIFFReadRGBAImageOriented -> pixReadFromTiffStream -> pixReadMemTiff -> pixReadMem`, and the upstream bridge stays inside the same OJPEG decode session named by the MSan allocation/store frames `OJPEGWriteHeaderInfo <- OJPEGDecodeRaw`.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Yes. Step 8 allocates the scratch buffer identified by MSan, step 10 is the libjpeg raw-data fill boundary for that allocation, step 11 copies a chroma byte from that allocation into the decoded strip, step 12 reads that strip byte as `Cb`, and step 13 consumes `Cb` at the crash site.

poc.trigger: The staged witness is a `pix_rotate_shear_fuzzer` input whose first 6 bytes are consumed as three int16 values and whose remaining bytes begin with the TIFF signature `II*\0` at byte offset 6. Running the harness on that exact buffer reproduces MemorySanitizer's use-of-uninitialized-value in `TIFFYCbCrtoRGB`.

format.name: pix_rotate_shear_fuzzer buffer with 6-byte prefix and TIFF payload
format.contract: The witnessed trigger is the staged buffer exactly in the shape reproduced here: six leading bytes consumed by the harness as angle, x_center, and y_center, followed immediately by a TIFF payload whose first four payload bytes are `49 49 2a 00` and whose OJPEG decode path reaches `gtStripContig`, `putcontig8bitYCbCr22tile`, and `TIFFYCbCrtoRGB`. This contract is limited to that observed witness shape and does not generalize to neighboring prefixes, alternate TIFF layouts, or other OJPEG files.
